_comment: The Trends role families, taxonomy v3 (ADR-0220): one axis, what the Job does. Language, level and employer are never a family; Java/Python and named sub-roles are watch roles. The list was drawn from the occupation standards surveyed in docs/role-families/2026-09-24_family-assignment-methods-research.md; two blind labellers then labelled 570 Jobs against a finer list, and the one pair they could not tell apart (ML engineering vs data science, kappa 0.41) was merged. A Job's family comes from its title, through the classifier in config/role_family_classifier/; its manifest's families must all appear here. unclassified-tech is where the classifier puts a title it cannot place with confidence. non-tech is reserved for the diagnostic series and is not listed. `definition` is the labelling rubric's line for the family, kept here for reviewers. Labels can be reworded freely: the ledger stores names. `retired` keeps the display labels of the families before ADR-0220, so the Space can still name the older series it serves while a new head's title cache warms up; nothing counts into them any more.

families.name: software-engineering
families.label: Software Engineering
families.definition: Builds software: backend, full stack, general application development, language-named developers, SDE, Member of Technical Staff, game, graphics, compiler and performance engineers, Forward Deployed Engineers.

families.name: frontend-web
families.label: Frontend & Web
families.definition: Builds what runs in the browser or a website: front-end, UI and web developers, React/Angular/Vue, CMS sites.

families.name: mobile
families.label: Mobile
families.definition: iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native and other mobile app development.

families.name: embedded-firmware
families.label: Embedded & Firmware
families.definition: Software that runs on devices: firmware, embedded C/C++, RTOS, BSP, device drivers, automotive and avionics software.

families.name: hardware-engineering
families.label: Hardware & Silicon
families.definition: Designs or verifies computing hardware: ASIC/FPGA/RTL, design verification, physical design, analog/RF IC, PCB and board design, silicon validation.

families.name: qa-test
families.label: QA & Test
families.definition: Tests software: QA, test automation, SDET, manual and performance testing.

families.name: devops
families.label: DevOps
families.definition: Builds and runs delivery tooling: DevOps and DevSecOps, CI/CD, build and release, infrastructure as code.

families.name: sre-platform
families.label: SRE & Platform
families.definition: Keeps production software reliable and gives developers a platform: site reliability, platform and production engineering, observability.

families.name: cloud-infrastructure
families.label: Cloud Infrastructure
families.definition: Builds and runs cloud infrastructure on AWS, Azure or GCP: cloud engineers, architects and administrators, migration and operations.

families.name: security
families.label: Security
families.definition: Cybersecurity of any kind: security engineering and analysis, SOC, penetration testing, AppSec, IAM, GRC, incident response.

families.name: data-engineering
families.label: Data Engineering
families.definition: Moves and stores data for others to use: pipelines, ETL/ELT, data platforms and warehouses, analytics engineering, data architecture.

families.name: database-administration
families.label: Database Administration
families.definition: Runs databases: DBAs, database reliability, backup and performance tuning.

families.name: ai-ml-data-science
families.label: AI, ML & Data Science
families.definition: Builds ML/AI systems or models data to learn or predict: ML and AI engineers, MLOps, LLM and GenAI engineers, data scientists, applied and research scientists.

families.name: data-analytics-bi
families.label: Data Analytics & BI
families.definition: Reports on data: data, BI and reporting analysts, BI developers, business and systems analysts in IT or data contexts.

families.name: enterprise-applications
families.label: Enterprise Applications
families.definition: Configures or extends packaged business software: SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Oracle applications, Workday, Dynamics and similar.

families.name: network-engineering
families.label: Network Engineering
families.definition: Builds and runs networks: network engineers and administrators, NOC, telecom and wireless networks.

families.name: systems-administration-it-operations
families.label: Systems Administration & IT Ops
families.definition: Runs IT systems: system administrators, Windows and Linux, M365 and Active Directory, endpoint management, data-centre operations.

families.name: it-support
families.label: IT Support
families.definition: Helps users with IT: help desk, desktop, service desk, technical and application support.

families.name: architecture
families.label: Architecture
families.definition: Designs systems across functions without one named function: solution, enterprise, technical and integration architects.

families.name: solutions-engineering
families.label: Solutions Engineering
families.definition: The technical side of selling or deploying a vendor's product: solutions, sales and pre-sales engineers, customer engineers, technical account managers.

families.name: systems-engineering
families.label: Systems Engineering
families.definition: Engineering of whole physical systems rather than software or IT: aerospace, defence, automotive and space systems engineering, MBSE, V&V.

families.name: product-management
families.label: Product Management
families.definition: Product managers and product owners of software or data products.

families.name: program-project-management
families.label: Program & Project Management
families.definition: Runs delivery: technical program and project managers, IT delivery managers, scrum masters, release managers.

families.name: engineering-management
families.label: Engineering Management
families.definition: Manages engineers or IT staff: engineering managers, directors and VPs of engineering, CTO, CIO, IT managers.

families.name: unclassified-tech
families.label: Unclassified tech
families.definition: Tech Jobs whose title the classifier cannot place with confidence.
